great_tartary_plains: The horizon refuses to settle. Aether moves under the grass like breath under a sheet.
Compasses turn here as if remembering an older north.
This is the wound itself. Centuries have not closed it.
Storms of violet and blue argue overhead in a tongue no one alive still speaks.
The plains keep the cataclysm fresh, the way mud keeps a footprint.
Time runs uneven here. A long stride may cost an hour. A short one may cost a year.
Walk softly. The ground above the buried cities is thin in places, and listening.
The wind here carries names. Most of them belong to nobody alive.
Old roads thread the grass, paved with stone that does not erode. The roads do not lead where they used to.
Reclaimers cross these plains in long quiet lines. They do not speak. The plains punish noise.
asgardar: The capital sleeps under Aetherstone, breathing through cracks no shovel can widen.
Once, the Grand Spire poured the heavens into these streets. The streets are still bright in places no light reaches.
Mud Monarch heralds still walk these avenues, though the avenues are buried and the heralds long dead.
Asgardar does not forget being a capital. It only forgets that the world above has moved on.
Listen at the right wall and the city grid still hums, faint as a heart through a closed door.
The Giants planned for everything except being remembered like this.
Coins of the old mint surface in the rubble. They are still warm.
Banners hang in chambers no one has unsealed. They are the right colours.
Aether circles Asgardar like a watcher who has not decided whether to enter.
The capital is patient. It outwaited an empire. It will outwait you.
yuldra_tul: Frost on the gate-arches, five centuries deep. Everywhere else the Flood came warm.
The tombs above the city are older than the city. The Servants say that is the correct order.
Your breath hangs in the passes. Something in the keep below is keeping the cold.
The vigil-braziers on the walls are unlit and unrusted, as if put out yesterday.
Snow settles on the drowned domes and does not melt. The mountain has opinions about time.
The gate-city let the Giants through all its history. It has not decided about you.
Ice rims the tomb-doors in patterns too regular to be weather. The Servants call them seals and bow.
The wind through the passes carries a low note that never quite resolves. The keep is humming to itself.
Rope-lines from the old vigil run wall to wall, knotted in the Servants' knots. They still hold weight.
Nothing scavenges here. The cold keeps the ruins honest.
ostragar: The current moves through the streets at walking pace, and has since the Flood. Nothing hurries here.
Reed-boats of the old Dynasty still ride at their moorings, waterlogged but unwilling to sink.
The still pool around the Core seat does not ripple. Throw a stone if you must. It won't.
Herons stand on the palace roofline. They were the river's court before the Dynasty and stayed after.
Every bridge in Ostragar is a low arch over slow water. The city was built to flood politely.
Somewhere under the current a cantor's chord is still holding. You can feel it in the bridge-rails.
Lantern-poles lean over the canals at the angle the current chose for them. The water decides things here.
The Dynasty's flood-marks climb the walls in neat painted lines. The top mark is the Flood. There is no line above it.
Fish move through the palace gates in slow schools, unbothered by rank.
Every mooring-ring in the city is polished bright. Something still ties up at night.
iskan_veil: The corridor you came in by is not behind you. This is normal here. Keep walking.
Every map of Iskan-Veil is wrong by design. The city considers this a courtesy.
Doors open onto brickwork; walls open onto streets. The Architects called it filing.
The far-northwestern light comes in flat and grey and lies about the hour.
Chalk your turnings if it comforts you. The chalk moves.
Somewhere in the maze is the door you didn't see. It is exactly where you'd never look, which is how you know it's real.
A staircase rises three floors and delivers you to the floor you left. Count again. It happened.
The Architects' sigil appears exactly once in the whole city, on a door that opens onto nothing. A signature.
Footsteps in the dust ahead of you, fresh, in your own boot-size. Walk on.
The city's one honest corridor is the one nobody has found.
karok_sa: Binding-sigils run the basalt halls in unbroken lines. Do not step on the lines.
The air tastes of cold iron and old ritual. The Order calls that clean.
Seals within seals within seals. A Sealwarden could read you the order they open in. None will.
The black stone drinks lantern-light and gives back less than it took.
Chant-echoes persist in the lower halls long after anyone chants. The halls are practicing.
The southern band buried every city it held. Karok-Sa it buried carefully.
A votive shelf runs the length of the processional hall — hundreds of small iron bells, none with a clapper.
The Order's masks watch from wall niches, eyeless and patient. They were carved watching.
Water finds its way even here, and comes out of the basalt tasting of ash and litany.
Somewhere below, a seal is holding. You can feel the effort of it through the floor.
tartarian_enclave: Mud walls shaped by Aethercraft, smooth as thrown clay. The Enclave was not dug; it was persuaded.
Ancestor-shrines to the fallen Giants line the galleries, each with a lamp that is someone's whole duty.
The Seekers go out into the tunnel-dark for relics and come back quieter each time.
Above you, the Buried Cities. Above those, the world. Depth is a kind of safety and the Enclave believes in it.
Strangers find the Sunken Enclave only when it decides to be found. You were decided about.
The tunnels breathe on a slow cycle, like something very large asleep further down.
Glow-moss lines the galleries in bands, farmed in rows. Light, down here, is agriculture.
A child's chalk game is drawn on the tunnel floor, rules unknowable, recently played.
The Enclave's records are knotted cords hung in the archive gallery. The archivist reads them with closed eyes.
Every passage narrows before it opens. The Enclave was built by people who understood arrivals.
parley_ground: A ring of standing stones and no walls. The absence of walls is the whole message.
The banners change with the season. The stones do not care whose.
Envoys' fires burn in the lee of the stones, spaced with surveyed exactness. Trust, measured in yards.
Every truce sworn here has been broken somewhere else. None has been broken here.
The flats around the ring hold no cover for an ambush. The site was chosen by someone who checked.
Words are the only weapon the ground permits. Sharpen accordingly.
The stones bear tally-scratches from bargains nobody alive remembers. The counting continues.
Rain pools in the same worn hollows where envoys have stood for centuries. The ground keeps minutes.
A broken sword lies at the ring's center, left as a term of some old accord. Rust has made it permanent.
The flats hear everything and repeat nothing. Better than most brokers.
monarch_waystation: The seneschal logs your name without asking it. The Monarchs' ledgers have their ways.
Silt-stiff banners crack in the wind like slow applause. The court has standards to keep, even here.
This is the last ordered ground. Past the toll-arch, the world stops filing paperwork.
The toll is small and the logging is the point. Someone always knows who went down the road.
Waystation coffee is bad in a way that has been standardized across the realm.
The ledger-hall holds names going back before the Flood. Some of the down-column names never came back up.
A Monarch clerk stamps a blank page, files it, and does not explain. Procedure survives content.
The toll-arch's inscription promises safe passage in the old tongue. The promise has outlived the safety.
Travelers' marks crowd the waystation posts — names, dates, arrows pointing down-road. Few arrows point back.
The seneschal's ledger lies open to today. The page is already half full.
dynasty_border_post: The garrison lamps are kept lit around the clock. The Dynasty does not explain to the dark.
The oath-stones stand where they were set, silt-scoured but readable. The oaths still scan.
Soldiers here polish armor no enemy will see. Discipline is the wall the Flood couldn't take.
The road past the post runs straight down into the flooded capitals. The garrison watches it like a wound.
Every Dynasty soldier walks that road once, going. The lucky ones walk it twice.
The border the post guards no longer exists. The guarding continues, and is somehow not absurd.
The watch-bell is rung at dusk whether anyone is watching or not. Especially then.
A Dynasty standard flies at full height, patched so many times the original cloth is a rumor.
The garrison's roll-call includes names no one answers to. They are called anyway, every morning.
Boot-prints in the mud parade ground, in formation, fresh each dawn.
pilgrim_waycamp: The fires are kept low and the songs lower. The road they rest for does not forgive noise.
Pilgrims mend boots and wills in the same firelight. Both need it before the descent.
Prayer-strips tied to the camp posts spell out names of the drowned cities, over and over.
The faithful sleep in rows aligned toward the Buried Cities. Even asleep, they are pointed.
An old pilgrim traces road-maps in the ash with a stick, from memory, correctly.
Nobody here calls the journey dangerous. They call it long, and let the word carry the weight.
A basin of clean water stands at the camp's edge for washing road-silt off before prayer. It is always full.
The pilgrims trade no goods, only routes — which descents held, which streets breathe.
A wall of small stones grows at the camp's south edge, one placed for each pilgrim who went down.
Songs here are hummed, not sung. The words are saved for below.
builders_survey_camp: Theodolite stakes march to the edge of the ruin-field and stop, like a sentence that thought better of itself.
Chalked plans cover the trestle-boards, revised nightly. The ground disagrees by morning.
Shoring timber stands stacked and numbered. The Builders trust arithmetic the way others trust prayer.
Past this camp the ground stops honoring measurements. The surveyors measure anyway, twice.
A level bubble sits dead center on the master bench. Everyone checks it on the way past. Ritual, or calibration. Both.
The camp's motto is chalked over the tool rack: MEASURE WHAT THE FLOOD LEFT.
A plumb-line hangs in a glass case at the camp's center, dead vertical. The Builders check it like a shrine.
Rejected survey pegs pile by the gate, each tagged with why the ground refused it.
The night shift plots stars against the ruin-line. Even the sky gets measured here.
Chalk dust on every sleeve. Arguments in right angles.
giant_watch_shrine: The keepers wait and watch. Ask what for and they offer you tea.
The shrine stone is worn smooth where five centuries of hands have rested, all at the same height.
Offerings here are practical: rope, lamp-oil, a whetstone. The Giants respected usefulness.
The vigil has not been broken since the Flood. Shifts change without a word.
From the shrine the road runs down toward the giant vaults, and the keepers watch it the way sailors watch weather.
At night the keepers bank the fire and sit facing the dark. Not fear. Manners.
The shrine's bell has no rope. If it rings, the keepers say, pulling it will not have been the cause.
Offerings left overnight are gone by morning. The keepers do not take them. They are certain of this.
A stone bench faces down-road, worn to a polish. Watching is done sitting here, correctly.
The vigil-fire burns low and blue on nights the keepers call listening nights.
revivalist_field_camp: The printing trestle runs half the night. Truth, the Revivalists say, has a deadline.
The map-board is stuck with pins and headlines-to-be. Some of the pins are hopes.
Ink and silt get everywhere here, in that order.
Diggers come in with crates; typesetters send out broadsheets. The camp is a machine for turning mud into news.
Every crate is stenciled EVIDENCE until proven otherwise.
They read the day's proofs aloud at the fire, arguing over every word. The arguing is the quality control.
Yesterday's broadsheet is nailed to the notice-post, corrections already inked in the margin.
The press-tender sleeps beside the trestle with one hand on the frame, like a carter with a nervous horse.
Crates leave the camp stamped TRUTH, EN ROUTE. The Revivalists do not consider this dramatic.
A wall of rejected headlines papers the mess tent. Morale, and a style guide.
reclaimer_stake: Claim-posts driven in rows, each one a bet against the mud. The Guild plays long odds on purpose.
The tally-board lists marked ruins in grease-pencil: DUG, DIGGING, DEEP, LATER. 'Later' is doing heavy work.
The winch rig groans all day. What comes up on the hook decides the evening's mood.
Everything here smells of rope, oil and wet earth — the Guild's incense.
Expeditions leave at first light, loud with gear. They come back at dusk, quiet with weight.
The western frontier starts at the last claim-post. The Guild keeps moving the post.
New hires learn the winch first and the tally-board second. Everything else, the mud teaches.
A claim-post snapped clean in half is displayed over the gate. Nobody explains it. Everybody understands it.
The Guild pays out at dusk by lamplight, coin counted twice, grudges counted once.
Maps here are working documents: mud-stained, re-inked, argued over, believed.
architect_blind: From the road: a collapsed waystation, not worth a second look. The second look is the test.
Behind the false rubble, a map-wall of routes the public must never connect. The strings are taut.
The quiet door onto the road opens without a sound. It was built to, and maintained to.
Watchers rotate on a schedule written nowhere. Everyone arrives on time anyway.
The blind sees everything that moves on the western road and files it. Filing is the Architects' violence.
You were watched from the moment the waystation looked abandoned. That is what the abandonment is for.
The rubble is arranged. Look long enough and the arrangement looks back.
A kettle in the back room is always warm. No fire is ever seen lit.
The map-wall's strings converge on places that are not marked. The marks are the part they show you.
Two travelers pass on the road and only one of them is logged. The blind knows which one mattered.
hidden_market: Four canvas stalls and no sign. If you found it, someone meant you to.
Agents of every faction trade here under an unspoken truce. Speaking it would end it.
No ledger, no names, no questions. Prices are memory and memory is excellent.
The wind off the Middens covers conversation three stalls away. The site was chosen for that.
Anything can be bought here once, and anyone forgiven twice. The third time is policy.
Write the market down on a map and the market moves. It has moved eleven times.
A stall sells maps of everywhere except here. Best sellers.
Prices drop at dusk and rise at rumor. The market has its own weather.
The four stalls have never been five. Expansion, the traders say, is how markets get found.
Someone pays in pre-Flood coin and no one blinks. Currency is anything that keeps its word.
grand_spire_of_asgardar: Fourteen tiers of it stand clear of the silt. Nobody has counted what is under.
The collector ring at the crown still turns, one degree an hour, tracking something that is no longer there.
From the base you cannot see the capital. That was the point of building it out here.
The stair goes up inside the wall. It was never meant for people, and it shows.
Something heavy shifts its weight on a landing far above and then settles again.
Snapped a third of the way up, and still the note comes down the shaft — under hearing, over the teeth.
The last streets of Asgardar stop a mile short of it, as if the city agreed to keep its distance.
Aether-light crawls the channel-grooves like slow lightning that forgot how to strike.
Rope left by earlier climbers hangs at the fourth tier. It has been there a long time. It is still good.
The warden has not left the stair. It is not clear it can.
black_reach: The ground simply stops. There is no lip, no warning, no ruin at the edge — only an end.
Heat comes up out of it, and with the heat a hum you feel in the soles of the feet before the ears find it.
Every other road into the Deep is a door. This one is a floor that gave out.
Drop a stone and count. You will lose interest before it lands.
There is no guardian here. Whatever this is, nobody built it to be kept.
The Mud Flood Nexus sits directly above, and the Reach seems to be listening to it.
Two miles west along the floor, something enormous is still standing. The light off it is wrong.
The walls are glassed smooth in places, as if the ground was opened fast and hot.
Cold air pours in over the edge and never comes back out.
This is the southernmost thing in the world. After it there is only down.
grand_spire_of_etheria: The Spire still drinks. From what celestial well, no one will answer.
Stand near its base and the Aether tightens around the chest, polite and proprietary.
Light moves up the inside of the tower in slow tides. It has its own schedule.
This was the throat of an empire. It is not entirely silent.
The Aetherborn feel the Spire before they see it. Some weep without knowing why.
Whatever the Spire was built to ground, it grounds it still.
Birds detour around the Spire's air column. The detour is wide. The birds are wise.
A single stone removed from the Spire weighs more in the hand than it did in the wall.
The Spire's shadow falls in the wrong direction at noon. No one comments on this anymore.
Climb the Spire only with intent. The Spire grades intent at every landing.
It drank the sun by day and the cold black sky by night, and gave the heat it could not use back to the stars. The radiators are dark now. The heat had to go somewhere.
samarran: The research city. The hum here is not metaphor.
Samarran does not rest. The walls are still working on Zalmar's last problem.
The mud arrived first to the laboratories. It learned things on the way in.
Diagrams ghost across the stone when the light is wrong. They redraw themselves if watched.
Every street here was a paper. The flood was the eraser. Some paragraphs survived.
Aetherons move thicker through Samarran's air. Lungs notice before minds do.
Glass vessels rest unbroken in the rubble. Some of them are still warm to the touch.
The university bell rings once a year, at no hour anyone has thought to record.
Scholars from the Order pilgrimage here. They do not all come back, but the ones who do come back changed.
An equation chalked on a wall here is older than every living language and still legible.
thametans_tower: The Engine is still in there. So is its mistake.
The walls hum at the frequency of the cascade. After a while, your bones learn the note.
Zalmar's last breath did not leave this tower. Few breaths do.
Touch nothing without need. Need will arrive uninvited.
This is where Tartaria asked the Aether for too much. The Aether has not finished answering.
Time pools on the upper floors. A minute spent there is rarely a minute when you leave.
The Aetheric Engine sleeps the way wounded animals sleep, with one eye open.
Brass valves on the lower levels turn themselves a quarter inch every century. Someone is counting.
Notes in Zalmar's hand are still pinned to the doors. The ink has not faded. The advice still applies.
Stairwells here loop in ways stairwells should not. Mark your steps.
The seals that fed the tower's heat to the sky cracked here first. You can still find the frost-line on the radiators where the cold stopped coming and the world caught fire instead.
voronov: Voronov was struck deepest. The flood found it on an ordinary morning.
Caches lie beneath this scar, intact, waiting for the right hand or the wrong one.
Houses here are whole, in their fashion, only inverted into the mud.
Reclaimers love Voronov. Voronov is patient with them, until it is not.
Aetherstone here is thinner in places. A pickaxe might break through. A foot certainly will.
The city kept its layout under the mud. Walk Voronov above-ground and you walk it below as well.
Lanterns in the lower city still flicker when the mud shifts. No one is lighting them.
Voronov's bell tower is upside down and ringing rarely. The bell is intact.
Children's toys surface here more often than coins. The mud is a strange editor.
Walk near the canals and the mud thins to slick clear water. Do not look down for long.
nimari: Half-swallowed. The half that remains has stopped pretending it is whole.
The Red Tower watches the plains. Faction banners change at its foot. The Tower does not.
Nimari's upper streets still hold roofs, doors, the suggestion of windows. Below, the mud is decisive.
Aetheric Cores hum at frequencies the body mistakes for hunger. Notice when you are not actually hungry.
The Mud Monarchs were born here, as much as they were born anywhere.
Listen for the bells. Nimari had bells, once. They sometimes remember.
Faction agents pass each other in Nimari's plazas without acknowledging the other exists. It is a small etiquette.
The cracked statues here still bleed Aether when the storms come close.
Doors in Nimari open inward, even the ones built to open out. The mud rewrote them.
Half a city is more than enough city for what walks here now.
red_tower_of_nimari: Red because of what the Aether did to its stone. Not because of paint.
A Core still beats in this tower. Every faction can hear it. So can you.
Climb only as high as your purpose. The Tower measures intent at each landing.
Sentinels patrol the inner stair, when they remember they are patrolling.
The light inside the Red Tower has weight. Stand under it long enough and you will feel it.
Many have reached the Core chamber. Few have left it the same.
Bloodlines older than the mud still match the Tower's locks. Newer hands meet older bolts.
The Tower's windows do not face outward. They face inward, into rooms that should not exist.
Aether condenses on the upper landings into thin red dew. It evaporates if breathed on.
Faction banners are tied at the Tower's foot every season. The Tower lets them rot in its own time.
varakush: The Forgotten Order keeps a door open here for those who know how to knock.
Lamps burn steady in Varakush. Steady lamps are rare in Tartaria. Notice them.
The library is older than the stronghold. The stronghold was built to protect the library.
Voices stay low here, not from fear, but from habit. Knowledge dislikes noise.
Rest is permitted. The Order's patience is finite, but it is genuine.
Tea, here, is a small ritual against the Aether. Drink the tea.
Scrolls in the deeper stacks reorder themselves when the moon is low. The librarians have stopped objecting.
Apprentices walk in pairs and write everything down. The Order remembers what gets written.
The kitchen here serves bread that does not stale. The recipe is not for the asking.
Varakush is one of the few places in Tartaria where the floor is reliably flat.
drakova: A Lost Capital. Lost means sealed, not destroyed. There is a difference.
Drakova waits the way old contracts wait: precisely, and with interest accruing.
The Aetherstone over Drakova is denser than the rest. Whatever is below was worth burying twice.
Some say a Core sleeps intact under Drakova. Some say it dreams.
The runes on the outermost stones have not weathered. The weather does not bother them.
Stand quietly. Drakova answers questions you have not yet thought to ask.
The Mud Monarchs were forbidden from Drakova by an older treaty than they admit to. They observe it.
Lamps here will not light. The dark is policy.
Drakova's gates are intact. They have not been opened since the mud arrived. They are not locked.
Walk Drakova's perimeter and your shadow walks a step behind, not below. Look once and then stop looking.
obsidian_pillars: The Pillars hate machines. Bring nothing that ticks if you mean to leave with it.
Black, polished, magnetic. They were aimed at something in the sky.
The observatory beneath the Pillars charted skies that no longer exist as charted.
Walk between two Pillars and your compass forgets you for a moment. Sometimes a long moment.
Birds will not perch here. Birds are wise.
The Pillars hum when the Aether storms come. They are the first to know.
Touch a Pillar with a bare hand and you will hear your own name in a voice you do not know.
The Pillars throw no shadow at noon. They throw two at dawn.
Aether collects in the basin between them like meltwater. It is not water. Do not drink.
Old maps marked the Pillars with a star. Old maps were not being polite.
endless_stair: Down, and down, and then a layer that refuses descent.
The Stair was built to be walked. It was not built to be reached.
Each step has been counted by someone. None of them agree on the number.
Aetheric pressure builds with depth. Past a certain landing, breath becomes a decision.
What is at the bottom is, in some sense, also at the top. The Stair confuses such distinctions.
Many have begun the descent. The Stair does not keep records, and neither does the mud below.
The Stair's walls are warm at the lower turns. Something below them is alive enough to give off heat.
Voices echo upward more easily than downward here. Speak quietly. Be heard quieter still.
Some steps have been worn smooth by feet. Others have not been stepped on by anything at all.
The lamps in the Stair are not lit by lamplighters. They light when needed. They are needed less often than you would think.
zharaks_teeth: Spires like a jawbone in shallow water. The water is shallow only at first.
Beautiful, by Tartarian standards. That has always been a warning.
Mud sirens nest in the highest spires. Their song is older than language and uses it anyway.
Do not answer what you hear here. Answers are how the Teeth feed.
The architecture rewards a quiet eye. The mud rewards a quiet foot.
At low tide, the Teeth show a little more. They never show all of themselves.
Boats wrecked on the Teeth do not surface. The Teeth do not return what they accept.
Aether storms gather here as if drawn by the architecture itself.
Each spire is hollow. Each spire is full. Both are true at different hours.
The Teeth were named by someone who survived them long enough to name them. That person did not return a second time.
sinking_cathedral: Only the steeple remains above the mud, and the steeple is leaning toward the listener.
The Cathedral keeps an artifact. The artifact keeps the Cathedral.
No one has returned. This is the cleanest statistic in Tartaria.
Bells should not still ring under mud. These do, occasionally, at no hour in particular.
Enter only if you have made peace with the possibility of staying.
The doors are open. The doors have always been open. That is the trap.
The pews below the mud are arranged for a service that has not adjourned.
Stained glass survives here in places it should not. The light through it falls on no one.
The Cathedral's clock has no hands. The clock keeps time anyway.
Faction priests of every banner refuse to bless this place. They do not refuse to acknowledge it.
cradle_of_dusk: The sky here is bruised with old Aether. It glows at hours that are not dusk.
Ships lie where the storms left them, crews intact, frozen mid-gesture.
Walk among the statues. Do not touch them. They were people, very recently in their own time.
The Cradle remembers the cascade as a single long moment, still happening.
Compass and clock will both surrender here. Bring patience instead.
What is dusk in the Cradle has been dusk for a long while. It is not waiting for night.
Aether lightning sketches itself across the air like a hand recalling a face.
Time pools here in basins. Step into one carefully and you may step out a different age.
The wind brings voices but never weather. Notice the difference.
Children's drawings, painted on stone, line the cliff walls. They are recent, by Cradle reckoning.
mud_seas: The Mud Seas are not sea, and not mud, and not still.
Currents move here without water moving. The Aether is the tide.
Whatever swims below was once something else. The mud was a long lesson.
Storms gather without sky. They arrive in the bones first.
Boats float here only by agreement. The agreement is renegotiated constantly.
A Leviathan's eye, kept dry, sees through these storms. Few keep such eyes.
The Mud Seas drown loud voices first. Yours, so far, has been careful.
Islands surface and submerge by Aether's whim. Maps are rewritten on the boats themselves.
Fish here have learned to walk, and most of them have forgotten how to swim.
The horizon does not flatten across the Mud Seas. It tilts. Notice when it tilts toward you.
giant_vault: The Giants lie here. Whether they sleep or are kept asleep is the question.
The Vault was sealed from the inside. That detail is rarely repeated.
Stand close to the door and the air tightens, as if a great chest were drawing breath.
The relics within outweigh kingdoms. The Giants within outweigh the relics.
Tartaria buried much. It locked very little. The Vault is one of the few.
If they wake, the question of who imprisoned whom will become urgent.
The True Tartarians do not approach the Vault. Their reverence does not require proximity.
Carvings on the Vault doors depict no events. They depict pauses between events.
Aether stops at the Vault's threshold as if asked politely.
The Vault's lock has no keyhole. It was never meant to be opened from outside.
mud_flood_nexus: This is the room where the disaster was managed, or could have been.
Touching the console here is not a small act. It is the act.
The Nexus has waited centuries to be addressed. It will answer.
Restoration and ruin sit on the same dial. The dial does not label them.
Every faction wants this room. The room has wanted, for some time, to be wanted differently.
Whatever happens here happens to Tartaria. Whatever happens to Tartaria happens to the world.
Decide slowly. The Aether keeps the minutes.
Brass levers here have been left in the position Zalmar last set them. No one has tried the second position.
The chamber's lighting follows the operator with quiet attention. It is not eager.
An inscription above the central console reads simply: not a wish.
etheric_chamber: The heart of it. The actual heart.
Automatons walk the Chamber's outer rings. They have not been relieved of their duty. They have not asked to be.
The traps here were designed by Tartarians at their cleverest. Their cleverest was considerable.
Aether sits thick in this air. Words slow. Thoughts slow. Both should be careful which way they finish.
The Chamber recognises a Tartarian bloodline. It is less courteous with strangers.
Light here is not lit. It is permitted.
Few have stood in this room with intact intent. Fewer have left with it.
The walls record what is said in this chamber. Whether the walls share what they record is its own question.
Each ring of the Chamber is colder than the last, and each ring is louder.
The Aetheric Chamber does not echo. It absorbs.
tartarian_outskirts: The borderlands. Where Tartaria thins, but does not stop.
Traps lie dormant in the grass, polite as sleeping dogs.
An expedition can die well here, and learn most of Tartaria's lessons in the process.
The Outskirts are kind to the careful and patient with the rest, briefly.
Aetheric anomalies pass through here on their way somewhere worse.
Markers, broken stones, half-buried signs. The Outskirts were once labeled.
Reclaimer caravans cut their own paths through these flats — no path holds for long.
A road here will end without warning, into mud or into Aether or into nothing at all.
Smoke columns rise on the horizon for hours and then are simply not there.
The Outskirts are where Tartaria practices being itself. The rehearsal is honest.
buried_cities: The buried cities sealed themselves under the same mud that killed them. There is no contradiction.
Time runs differently above each city. The map does not record this.
Aetherstone closed over these places like a verdict.
Below the seal, the streets are intact and the lamps are not entirely out.
Every buried city is a question Tartaria has not stopped asking.
Walk between cities and the air changes flavour. Each city was a different argument.
Excavation is not the only way in. Some doors are made of weather, or grief, or attention.
A buried city's name is heavier than the city itself. Speak names sparingly.
The seals are not all the same age. Some are still cooling.
Reclaimers have a saying: you do not unbury a city. You wait for it to remember itself.
raiders_ridge: Wind combs the scrub sideways. Every third rock carries a mark somebody meant to be read.
A cold firepit, stones still stacked to break the wind. Whoever sat here watched the outpost lights.
The ridge line gives you the whole borderland at a glance — and gives anyone on it your silhouette.
A tally is scratched into the lookout rock. Eleven strokes, then a twelfth in a different hand.
Loose stone turns under your boot and clatters a long way down. If anyone is near, they heard it.
The spiral-marks get fresher the higher you climb. Somebody keeps this ground marked on purpose.
Two cairns flank the path up, built with care by hands that expected to come back this way.
Dry lightning walks the horizon east of the ridge. Nothing out there for it to hit but you.
A snare line runs between two rocks at ankle height, old enough to trust, new enough not to.
The wind carries a smell of cold iron and horse — hours old, maybe less. You are not first today.
From the ridge top the outpost's lamps look close enough to shout at. Sound doesn't carry back.
Someone has ground a blade against the lookout rock so many times the stone has a wave in it.
vault_steps: The steps are cut for strides longer than yours. Climbing them is a conversation with giants.
Mud seeps between the stones and quivers, faintly, in time with something far below.
A toppled statue lies across the landing, face down, as if it chose not to watch the doors.
The seal-glyphs above the Vault doors glow faintly when the wind drops. They are not for you.
Bone shards stud the silt drifts — old wardens, or old visitors. The steps do not say which.
The trembling underfoot stops all at once, which is somehow worse than when it was going.
The mud between the lower steps holds a boot print with six toes. You stop counting yours.
High on the doors the seal-work throws back your lantern in colors stone has no business owning.
Every landing has a lip worn glassy by something dragged over it, always downward, never up.
A hairline crack crosses three steps in a straight line. It is warm to the touch, and it hums.
The last daylight leaves the stair early — the Vault's shadow reaches out to take it back.
Nothing nests here. On a stair this old, in mud this rich, that is its own kind of warning.
drowned_quarter: Roofs break the waterline like stepping stones. Under them, whole streets hold their breath.
The reeds move against the current. You stop poling until they stop moving.
A mooring post wears three ropes, all cut, all the same length. Nobody came back for the rafts.
Somewhere under the water a bell shifts in its drowned tower, a note more felt than heard.
The quiet here is worked — a silence with a shape to it, like a held throat.
Waterline doors stand ajar on their flooded rooms. Nothing swims out. Something could.
A kitchen window slides past under the raft, table still set, four bowls, forty years of silt.
The pole finds a rooftop, then a chimney, then nothing at all for a long, patient moment.
Reed stems close behind the raft like a door being drawn shut without hurry.
Something bumps the hull once, gently, from below — polite, almost, like a knock.
The waterline on the tallest building shows three floods, each one higher than the last.
A child's kite is still snagged on a drowned weathervane, string trailing down into the dark.
